tests.title: LiteRT matmul peak
tests.description: Matrix-multiply rate on this accelerator, one model format per row: sixteen chained square matmuls in one dispatch, swept over layer width and reported at its best. Each row names the kernel that ran, and a format LiteRT hands back to the CPU reports unsupported.

metrics.description: Full 32-bit precision, unless the numeric-error row says otherwise. Fastest at 2048-wide layers through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
16-bit weights and arithmetic. Fastest at 2048-wide layers through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
The GPU's fp16 policy with fp32 accumulation. Fastest at 2048-wide layers through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.

metrics.reason: LiteRT could not compile the model for the GPU: LiteRT status 3 (input->type != kTfLiteFloat32 (BFLOAT16 != FLOAT32); Node number 1 (FULLY_CONNECTED) failed to prepare.)
metrics.description: bfloat16 weights and arithmetic.
Full-integer int8: 8-bit activations and weights. Fastest at 4096-wide layers as FULLY_CONNECTED with the GPU's 8-bit kernels through the IrModel pipeline, with float inputs and outputs.

metrics.reason: the GPU accelerator aborts the process on int16 tensors rather than declining them (LiteRT 2.2.0 and 2.3.0), so this format is not sent to it
metrics.description: Full-integer int16x8: 16-bit activations over 8-bit weights.
8-bit weights, one scale per output column, against float activations. Fastest at 4096-wide layers with the GPU's 8-bit kernels through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.

metrics.reason: the GPU accelerator's blockwise int4 weight conversion overruns its buffer (an 8-bit transpose microkernel reads and writes past the packed nibbles, LiteRT 2.2.0 and 2.3.0) and corrupts the heap, so this format is not sent to it
metrics.description: 4-bit weights in blocks of 32 against float activations.

metrics.reason: LiteRT could not compile the model for the GPU: LiteRT status 3 (filter->type != kTfLiteFloat32 (FLOAT8_E4M3FN != FLOAT32); Node number 1 (FULLY_CONNECTED) failed to prepare.)
metrics.description: 8-bit float (E4M3) weights, one scale per output column, against float activations.

tests.title: LiteRT convolution peak
tests.description: 2-D convolution rate on this accelerator at 256 channels -- a stride-2 3x3, a 1x1 and a depthwise 3x3 -- each swept over feature-map size and reported at its best. Set against the matmul rows, it shows how well this accelerator handles convolution.

metrics.description: Stride-2 3x3, full 32-bit precision. Fastest at a 512x512 feature map through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
1x1 (a matmul per pixel), full 32-bit precision. Fastest at a 512x512 feature map through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
Depthwise 3x3 (each channel on its own), full 32-bit precision. Fastest at a 128x128 feature map through the IrModel pipeline.
Stride-2 3x3, 16-bit weights and arithmetic. Fastest at a 512x512 feature map through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
1x1 (a matmul per pixel), 16-bit weights and arithmetic. Fastest at a 128x128 feature map through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
Depthwise 3x3 (each channel on its own), 16-bit weights and arithmetic. Fastest at a 512x512 feature map through the IrModel pipeline.
Stride-2 3x3, full-integer int8 with per-channel weights. Fastest at a 512x512 feature map with the GPU's 8-bit kernels through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
1x1 (a matmul per pixel), full-integer int8 with per-channel weights. Fastest at a 1024x1024 feature map without the GPU's 8-bit kernels through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.
Depthwise 3x3 (each channel on its own), full-integer int8 with per-channel weights. Fastest at a 1024x1024 feature map without the GPU's 8-bit kernels through the GraphFloat32 pipeline.

tests.title: LiteRT matmul numeric error
tests.description: How far each format's answer on a 1024-cubed matmul drifts from a double-precision reference, in parts per million. The reference multiplies the exact values this accelerator was given, so only the arithmetic and the width the answer was kept in remain.

metrics.description: Full 32-bit precision: hundreds of ppm would mean a narrower type was used. Other forms gave 1 ppm through the IrModel pipeline.
